intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, blending breathwork and asana with Bali's natural beauty. A deeply restorative and affordable experience perfect for yoga enthusiasts.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful stretches of coastline. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Local surf schools offer affordable 2-hour sessions with equipment included.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Start your morning at a traditional local market in Ubud selecting fresh spices, vegetables, and herbs, then head to an open-air kitchen to learn how to prepare 5–6 authentic Balinese dishes including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. A hands-on cultural and culinary immersion led by local chefs.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Spend several sessions over your 13-day stay at The Yoga Barn, one of Bali's most renowned wellness centers. Choose from daily drop-in classes in Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, or meditation. The lush jungle setting, world-class instructors, and community atmosphere make this a bucket-list experience for yoga lovers.

experiences.name: Nusa Penida Island Day Trip & Kelingking Beach
experiences.description: Take a fast boat from Sanur to Nusa Penida and visit the iconic Kelingking Beach — a dramatic cliff-top viewpoint shaped like a T-Rex with turquoise waters below. Snorkel at Crystal Bay, spot manta rays at Manta Point, and explore the raw, untouched beauty of this stunning island just off Bali's coast.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked airport shuttle or budget Grab taxi (~IDR 80,000–120,000) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour warung near the resort or a convenience store (Indomaret/Alfamart) — budget under IDR 30,000

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival simple. Confirm check-in details with the resort in advance since it's a late arrival. Exchange a small amount of cash at the airport for immediate needs.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, enjoy a slow morning walk along the beachfront directly from the resort. Watch the sunrise over the ocean and get oriented with the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest beach stretch on foot. Rent a surfboard or bodyboard from a local beach vendor (~IDR 50,000/hour) and try the waves, or simply relax on the sand. Visit a nearby local market to pick up snacks and essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. Head to a nearby warung (local Indonesian eatery) for a traditional dinner. Stroll along the beachside strip and enjoy the relaxed Bali night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Nasi goreng or bubur ayam at a local warung near the resort — ~IDR 25,000
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and grilled corn from a beach vendor — ~IDR 20,000
meals.dinner: Mie goreng or gado-gado at a budget warung — ~IDR 35,000

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag recovery is important. The warm summer weather (25°C) is perfect for a gentle beach introduction. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Join a free or donation-based morning beach yoga session (many local instructors offer these near beachfront areas at sunrise, ~06:00–07:30). This is a wonderful budget-friendly way to start your yoga journey in Bali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or scooter (~IDR 60,000–80,000/day for scooter) and explore the surrounding village and rice paddies. Visit a local temple nearby — most are free or request a small donation. Dress respectfully with a sarong.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beach for golden hour. Find a beachside café or warung with floor cushions and enjoy Bintang beer or fresh juice while watching the sunset. Explore the local night food stalls (kaki lima) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes and Bali coffee at a local café — ~IDR 30,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch plate (nasi campur) — ~IDR 25,000–35,000
meals.dinner: Sate lilit and steamed rice from a night food stall — ~IDR 30,000

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rentals require an international driving permit. If uncomfortable riding, use Grab for transport. Morning yoga on the beach is a highlight — check notice boards at the resort for local class listings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga practice — either self-guided on the beach at sunrise or attend a budget yoga class at a local shala (~IDR 80,000–120,000 drop-in). Focus on a Hatha or Vinyasa session to energize the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a popular nearby beach known for snorkeling. Rent snorkel gear (~IDR 40,000) and explore the underwater world. Many budget beach clubs allow non-members to use facilities with a minimum spend.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local night market (pasar malam) for authentic Balinese street food. Try various small dishes — pisang goreng, martabak, and fresh fruit juices. Budget-friendly and culturally immersive.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or smoothie bowl at a health café near the yoga shala — ~IDR 45,000
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood grilled at the beach — fish or prawns with rice — ~IDR 50,000
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — ~IDR 40,000 for multiple dishes

day_by_day.notes: Check local Facebook groups or resort notice boards for the best budget yoga studios. Snorkeling spots are best visited in the morning when the water is calmest — afternoon works too given the warm weather.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a famous Bali beach further afield (e.g., Padang Padang or Bingin Beach if in the south, or adjust based on resort location). Share a Grab ride with fellow travelers to split costs. Arrive early to claim a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax, swim, and explore the beach caves and rock formations. Watch local surfers ride the waves. Bring your own snacks and water to avoid overpriced beach vendor costs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Treat yourself to a budget Balinese massage from a local massage parlor on the beach strip (~IDR 80,000–100,000 for 60 minutes). End the evening with a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab fruit, bread, and peanut butter from a local minimart — ~IDR 20,000
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch or buy from a warung near the beach — ~IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Cap cay or tofu tempe dish at a vegetarian-friendly warung — ~IDR 30,000

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: always negotiate massage prices politely. Bring a reusable water bottle and fill up at the resort to avoid buying plastic bottles. July weather is dry and warm — ideal beach day.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and yoga on your own on the resort beach at sunrise. Practice breathwork (pranayama) and gentle stretching for 45–60 minutes. This is free and deeply restorative in the Bali ocean setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby cultural attraction — visit a traditional Balinese Hindu temple. Many temples are free or request a small entrance donation (~IDR 10,000–20,000). Learn about offerings, architecture, and local customs.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost Kecak fire dance performance if available nearby (~IDR 100,000 at major venues — worth the splurge). Alternatively, watch local cultural performances at community spaces.

meals.breakfast: Jaja Bali (traditional Balinese rice cakes) and black rice pudding from a local stall — ~IDR 20,000
meals.lunch: Babi guling (suckling pig) or vegetarian nasi campur at a famous local warung — ~IDR 40,000
meals.dinner: Simple fried rice and tempeh at a budget warung — ~IDR 25,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong and sash when entering temples — many provide them for free or for a small rental fee. The Kecak dance is a spectacular cultural experience unique to Bali.

day_by_day.morning: Midpoint of the trip — join a guided group yoga and meditation retreat day (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for a half-day program). Many budget retreat centers in Bali offer affordable packages including a light meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-yoga relaxation at the beach. Practice what you learned in the morning session — try a self-guided meditation sitting by the ocean. Journal your Bali experiences so far.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the halfway point with a slightly elevated budget dinner at a beachfront warung. Order fresh grilled fish, a local vegetable dish, and coconut water. Enjoy the stars over the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Included in the yoga retreat program or a simple smoothie — ~IDR 30,000
meals.lunch: Light post-yoga meal — tempeh, salad, and herbal tea — ~IDR 40,000
meals.dinner: Grilled fish with sambal, rice, and vegetables at a beachfront warung — ~IDR 60,000

day_by_day.notes: Research retreat centers in advance — Ubud is famous for yoga retreats but local areas near the resort may have hidden gems. Budget retreats often offer the same quality as luxury ones.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk collecting shells and watching fishing boats return with their catch. Chat with local fishermen — a genuinely authentic Bali experience at zero cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget cooking class (~IDR 150,000–200,000) to learn how to make traditional Balinese dishes like lawar, sate, and jamu (herbal drink). Many classes include a market visit.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or enjoy your cooking class meal. Spend the evening at the resort beach, stargazing and reflecting. The clear July skies make for excellent stargazing away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate (papaya, watermelon, pineapple) from a market stall — ~IDR 20,000
meals.lunch: Meal prepared during the cooking class — included in the class fee
meals.dinner: Leftovers from cooking class or a light warung meal — ~IDR 25,000

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are one of Bali's best budget activities — you eat what you cook! Book in advance or look for last-minute spots. Great way to bring Bali home with you.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga flow on the beach — this time try a slightly more challenging practice: sun salutations facing the ocean as the sun rises. If you'd like guidance, many beach yoga instructors offer informal sessions for tips (~IDR 50,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore tide pools and rocky outcrops along the coastline near the resort. Look for sea creatures, colorful fish, and coral. Bring snorkel gear for a closer look. This is free and endlessly fascinating.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local art market or craft fair. Browse handmade Balinese goods — wood carvings, silver jewelry, batik fabrics. Practice your bargaining skills. Budget ~IDR 50,000–100,000 for souvenirs if desired.

meals.breakfast: Roti bakar (toasted bread with local jam and butter) and Bali coffee — ~IDR 20,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — mixed rice with 3 toppings of your choice — ~IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Soup noodle dish (bakso or soto ayam) from a street cart — ~IDR 20,000

day_by_day.notes: Tide pool exploration is best at low tide — check tide charts for the day. Bargaining at markets is expected and part of the culture — start at 50% of the asking price and negotiate respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby waterfall or rice terrace (depending on your resort location in Bali). Share transport costs with other travelers. The lush greenery after the rainy season is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in the natural pool at the base of the waterfall or walk through the rice terraces. Take photos, breathe in the fresh air, and connect with Bali's natural interior landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub at a budget spa (~IDR 100,000). End the evening with a quiet dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Instant noodles or packaged breakfast from the minimart — ~IDR 15,000 (budget day)
meals.lunch: Warung near the waterfall — nasi goreng and bottled water — ~IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Simple tofu and tempe stir-fry with rice at a local warung — ~IDR 25,000

day_by_day.notes: Popular waterfalls like Tegenungan or Gitgit charge a small entrance fee (~IDR 15,000–20,000). Wear sturdy sandals or shoes for waterfall hikes. Bring insect repellent for jungle areas.

day_by_day.morning: Final dedicated yoga morning — practice a 90-minute session combining everything learned during the trip: pranayama, asana, and meditation. Do this on the beach at sunrise as a personal ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing at the beach — your last full beach afternoon. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) rented from a beach vendor (~IDR 80,000/hour) for something new and fun.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach bonfire if permitted, or join other travelers for a shared sunset viewing. Visit a rooftop bar or beachside café for one celebratory drink (Bintang beer ~IDR 35,000) to mark near-end of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Balinese breakfast at the resort or a café — nasi goreng, fruit, coffee — ~IDR 40,000
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut, grilled corn, and a fruit smoothie at the beach — ~IDR 35,000
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at a slightly nicer warung — order multiple local dishes to share — ~IDR 70,000

day_by_day.notes: Reflect on your yoga and beach journey. Consider writing in a travel journal about your highlights. Check your budget spending and allocate remaining funds for last-day activities and souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning beach walk and meditation. Collect any remaining souvenirs or gifts from local markets. Pack non-essential items to make the last day easier. Visit the resort beach one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon exploration — revisit your favorite spot from the trip, whether a beach, temple, or warung. Take final photos and soak in the Bali atmosphere. Chat with locals and fellow travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Final Bali dinner — go all out within budget. Order a spread of your favorite Balinese dishes discovered during the trip. Enjoy a final sunset and toast to an amazing 13-day adventure.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl and fresh juice at a health café — ~IDR 45,000
meals.lunch: Nasi campur at your favorite warung from the trip — ~IDR 35,000
meals.dinner: Best-of-Bali dinner spread: sate, lawar, nasi goreng, fresh fish, and coconut water — ~IDR 80,000

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transport in advance. A Grab taxi or shuttle (~IDR 80,000–150,000) is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option. Pack light and check baggage allowances.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach — a peaceful send-off ritual. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the front desk if departure is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, spend remaining hours at the nearest beach or explore a last local spot. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 2–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with incredible memories of beaches, yoga, culture, and budget-friendly adventures. Reflect on the journey and plan your return.

meals.breakfast: Final Bali breakfast — banana pancakes and Bali coffee at a beachside café — ~IDR 30,000
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a last warung stop near the resort — ~IDR 30,000
meals.dinner: Airport food or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Ngurah Rai Airport has limited budget food options — eat before arriving if possible. Duty-free shopping is available for last-minute gifts. Ensure you have no Balinese temple items in your luggage that may be restricted. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival — budget around IDR 80,000–150,000

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport pickup with the resort in advance. Keep travel documents and local currency (IDR) handy. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM for initial expenses. Rest well for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a gentle stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself with the surroundings and soak in your first Bali sunrise views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest beach area on foot. Rent a sun lounger, dip in the warm Indian Ocean, and acclimatize to Bali's warm summer weather (~25°C). Visit a nearby beachside warung for a refreshing coconut drink.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach followed by dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant near the resort. Enjoy fresh grilled seafood and local Balinese dishes.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or IDR 100,000–180,000
meals.lunch: Casual beachside warung — nasi goreng or mie goreng — IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant nearby — grilled fish, rice, and vegetables — IDR 120,000–220,000

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen regularly. This is an orientation day — no heavy touring needed.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a sunrise beach yoga session. Many resorts and nearby studios offer morning classes from 07:00–08:30. Check if Aegean Bliss Resort offers in-house yoga or book a session at a nearby studio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a local market or beach village for souvenir browsing and cultural immersion. Explore local crafts, sarongs, and handmade jewelry. Try a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa (budget: IDR 100,000–180,000 for 60 minutes).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance if available near your area (tickets ~IDR 100,000–150,000). Follow with dinner at a mid-range Indonesian restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local café — avocado toast or tropical fruit bowl — IDR 60,000–120,000
meals.lunch: Local warung near the market — sate lilit (Balinese satay) with rice — IDR 50,000–90,000
meals.dinner: Mid-range Indonesian restaurant — babi guling (suckling pig) or ayam betutu — IDR 100,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga class and Kecak performance in advance if possible. Wear comfortable clothing for both activities. Bring a sarong for cultural sites.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga practice on the beach at sunrise (self-guided or guided class). Afterward, enjoy a healthy smoothie bowl at a nearby café before heading out for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided snorkeling trip to nearby coral reefs. Many operators near the beachfront offer half-day snorkeling excursions (IDR 200,000–400,000 per person including equipment). Discover colorful marine life in Bali's warm coastal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, shower, and relax. Head out for a casual dinner at a beachside café. Watch the stars from the beach after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl café nearby — acai bowl or tropical smoothie — IDR 60,000–110,000
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or grab food at the snorkeling operator's base — sandwiches or local snacks — IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Beachside café — fresh tuna steak or calamari with salad — IDR 130,000–230,000

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling. Bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro from the operator. Confirm snorkeling trip the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud — hire a private driver for the day (IDR 400,000–600,000). Morning visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary. Stroll through the ancient temples and lush jungle paths surrounded by macaque monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud Art Market for handcrafted goods and paintings. Visit the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) exterior and surrounding streets. Enjoy lunch at a mid-range restaurant in central Ubud.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby spot. Optional: book a traditional Balinese reflexology session (IDR 80,000–150,000).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Ubud mid-range restaurant — Balinese rijsttafel (rice table set) — IDR 120,000–200,000
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby — mixed grill or nasi campur — IDR 100,000–190,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes for the Monkey Forest. Keep valuables secured as monkeys may snatch items. Hire a reputable driver through the resort for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session at the beach or resort. After yoga, take a leisurely morning swim in the ocean. Explore the hotel's beachfront and nearby coastline at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby surf school for a beginner or intermediate surfing lesson (IDR 250,000–450,000 for 2-hour lesson including board and instructor). Bali's warm summer waves are perfect for learning.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a beachfront bar. Watch the famous Bali sunset with a Bintang beer or fresh fruit cocktail. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Resort café — eggs benedict or full tropical breakfast — IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.lunch: Surf school area warung — gado-gado or fried rice — IDR 40,000–75,000
meals.dinner: Ocean-view mid-range restaurant — grilled prawns with coconut rice — IDR 140,000–250,000

day_by_day.notes: Inform the surf instructor of your experience level. Wear rash guard for sun protection. Surfing conditions in July are generally excellent with consistent swells.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and wellness morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time journaling or reading on the beach. Optional: book a 90-minute Balinese massage at the resort spa (IDR 200,000–350,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby temple or local village on foot or by scooter rental (IDR 60,000–100,000/day). Visit a local temple during the afternoon when it's less crowded. Observe traditional Balinese Hindu offerings and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience — join a local Balinese cooking class (IDR 300,000–500,000) where you learn to prepare traditional dishes like lawar, satay, and black rice pudding. Dinner is the meal you cook!

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, and local coffee — IDR 70,000–130,000
meals.lunch: Light café lunch — club sandwich or salad — IDR 60,000–110,000
meals.dinner: Your own Balinese cooking class creations — included in class fee

day_by_day.notes: Midpoint rest day — intentionally lighter schedule. Book cooking class in advance as popular classes fill up quickly. Wear a sarong and sash when visiting temples.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga on the beach at sunrise followed by a healthy breakfast. Head out for a day trip to Tanah Lot Temple — one of Bali's most iconic sea temples perched on a rock formation (entrance ~IDR 60,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Tanah Lot, explore the surrounding area and coastal cliffs. Visit nearby Batu Bolong Temple or browse local art galleries and shops in the Tanah Lot area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at a local restaurant. Optional: rooftop or beachfront bar for evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurant near Tanah Lot — mixed Indonesian dishes — IDR 80,000–160,000
meals.dinner: Local mid-range restaurant near resort — bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck) — IDR 120,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Visit Tanah Lot during low tide for the best views and access. Arrive early to avoid crowds. Wear a sarong (available for rent at the site). Sunset views here are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga session. Afterward, explore a different beach nearby — rent a scooter or hire a driver to visit a quieter, less touristy beach for a change of scenery and peaceful swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Paddleboarding or kayaking session along the coastline (IDR 100,000–200,000/hour rental). Enjoy the calm afternoon waters and coastal views from the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Beachside bonfire or sunset dining experience. Choose a restaurant that offers open-air beachfront seating. Try a seafood barbecue platter.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie café — green smoothie and granola — IDR 70,000–120,000
meals.lunch: Beachside warung at the quiet beach — fresh coconut, spring rolls, and fried fish — IDR 50,000–90,000
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood BBQ restaurant — mixed seafood platter — IDR 150,000–280,000

day_by_day.notes: Check tide and weather conditions before paddleboarding. Wear a life jacket provided by the rental operator. Explore neighboring beaches for variety — each has its own character.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the rice terraces — visit the stunning UNESCO-listed Tegallalang Rice Terraces near Ubud. Walk along the terraced paths and enjoy the lush green landscape. Best visited in the morning before it gets crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a local coffee plantation for a Luwak coffee tasting experience (IDR 50,000–150,000). Learn about the coffee-making process and sample Bali's famous brews. Browse local handicraft villages on the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Relaxing evening with dinner at a cozy mid-range restaurant. Optional: evening beach walk and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Warung at Tegallalang — nasi goreng with egg — IDR 50,000–90,000
meals.dinner: Cozy mid-range restaurant near resort — wood-fired pizza or pasta for variety — IDR 100,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the rice terrace paths. Bring a hat and sunscreen. Some sections of the terrace walk may charge a small entrance fee (IDR 10,000–20,000). Morning light makes for excellent photography.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session — make the most of your remaining days. After yoga, enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning relaxing by the pool or beach with a book.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wellness center for a full spa afternoon — choose from treatments like a Balinese body scrub, flower bath, and deep tissue massage. Budget IDR 300,000–500,000 for a multi-treatment package.
day_by_day.evening: Special mid-range dinner at a nicer restaurant — celebrate the near-end of the trip with a slightly elevated dining experience. Try a restaurant offering both Indonesian and international fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort breakfast — eggs any style, fresh juice, tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the spa or nearby café — salad and fresh juice — IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Fusion restaurant — tasting menu or à la carte — IDR 200,000–350,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa package in advance for preferred time slots. This is a dedicated rest and rejuvenation day — fully embrace the wellness theme of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the ocean one last time. Bring a journal to reflect on the trip. Optional: early morning meditation on the beach at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a nearby market or beach stalls. Pick up Balinese sarongs, essential oils, local coffee, or handmade jewelry as gifts. Bargain respectfully at local markets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset dinner at your favorite beachfront restaurant from the trip. Order your favorite Balinese dishes and enjoy the warm evening ambiance. Toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy the full spread one last time
meals.lunch: Casual warung near the market — last taste of local street food — IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Favorite beachfront restaurant revisited — celebratory dinner — IDR 150,000–280,000

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essential items tonight to make the final morning easier. Keep important documents, electronics, and valuables in carry-on bags. Confirm airport transfer for departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach if time permits. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange resort transfer or private driver to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before flight for check-in, immigration, and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Bali souvenirs or Luwak coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Carry wonderful memories of 13 days of beaches, yoga, culture, and Balinese warmth.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — IDR 80,000–150,000
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00–12:00 — confirm with the resort. Store luggage at the hotel if you have free time before your flight. Keep IDR for airport tips and last purchases. Arrival tax and departure taxes are typically included in your ticket.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. A private luxury transfer in an air-conditioned vehicle will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night amenity prepared by the resort. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind to the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity and curated snack platter arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Request the resort's private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with the concierge. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk along the resort's private beach, soaking in the warm Bali morning air (avg. 25°C). Book a 60-minute sunrise yoga session on the beach pavilion with the resort's resident yoga instructor – a perfect gentle start to recalibrate after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool and private beach. Arrange a luxury 90-minute 'Balinese Welcome' massage at the resort spa – incorporating warm volcanic stones and traditional herbal compresses. Explore the resort grounds, gardens, and beachfront at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's beach bar. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant, savoring a curated tasting menu of modern Indonesian cuisine paired with premium wines.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront restaurant – fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, freshly squeezed juices, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's cabana bar – grilled seafood, fresh salads, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Signature tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort's fine-dining restaurant – modern Indonesian cuisine with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the spa treatment and yoga session through the resort concierge. This is a recovery day – keep it resort-based and relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a 7:00 AM sunrise yoga and pranayama session on the private beach – the warm, calm July morning makes this ideal. After yoga, enjoy a nourishing breakfast. Then take a private guided tour to the iconic Tanah Lot Temple, one of Bali's most sacred sea temples, perched dramatically on a coastal rock formation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Beraban Village to experience traditional Balinese culture and artisan crafts. Return to the resort for a refreshing swim and a private 'Jamu' herbal wellness ritual at the spa – a traditional Balinese health elixir treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort – a candlelit table on the sand with a personalized menu crafted by the head chef, featuring fresh local seafood and premium ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Healthy superfood breakfast bowl, fresh papaya, Balinese black rice porridge, and specialty coffee at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium local restaurant near Tanah Lot – try Tapa Restaurant or a similar upscale venue with ocean views and fresh Balinese cuisine
meals.dinner: Private beachfront candlelit dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – personalized 5-course menu with sommelier-selected wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the Tanah Lot private guided tour through the concierge. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring a sarong for temple entry. July weather is excellent – minimal rain expected.

day_by_day.morning: Morning vinyasa yoga flow class at 7:30 AM at the resort's clifftop or beachfront yoga shala. After yoga, embark on a private guided snorkeling or paddleboarding excursion along Bali's crystal-clear coastal waters near the resort – the calm July seas are perfect for water activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter for an afternoon coastal cruise along Bali's southwestern coastline. Swim in secluded coves, enjoy champagne on deck, and take in views of the dramatic Balinese shoreline. Return to the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby premium beach club (such as Finns Beach Club or Sundara at Four Seasons Jimbaran) for sundowners, ambient DJ sets, and a sophisticated cocktail experience overlooking the Indian Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Healthy açaí bowl, avocado toast, tropical fruit platter, and cold-pressed juices at the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed on the private boat charter – artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, tropical fruits, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sundara at Four Seasons Jimbaran or equivalent luxury beach club – fresh Jimbaran Bay seafood, oysters, and premium cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2 days in advance through the concierge. Life jackets and snorkeling equipment provided. SPF 50+ sunscreen recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning 6:30 AM meditation and yin yoga session on the beach. After breakfast, take a private chauffeured excursion to Uluwatu – explore the stunning Uluwatu Temple perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean on a dramatic clifftop. Enjoy breathtaking panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Padang Padang Beach or Bingin Beach – two of Bali's most beautiful and pristine beaches. Relax on the white sand, swim in the turquoise waters, and enjoy the relaxed surfer-chic atmosphere. Visit a premium beach café for a refreshing break.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset – one of Bali's most iconic cultural experiences, performed against a backdrop of the setting sun over the ocean. Afterward, dine at Sundays Beach Club or Ulu Cliffhouse for a premium clifftop dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and Balinese herbal teas
meals.lunch: Lunch at Single Fin Uluwatu or equivalent premium beach café – fish tacos, fresh salads, smoothie bowls, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ulu Cliffhouse or Sundays Beach Club – contemporary international cuisine with dramatic Indian Ocean views and curated cocktail list

day_by_day.notes: The Kecak Dance begins around 18:00 – arrive 30 minutes early for good viewing spots. Sarong required for Uluwatu Temple entry (provided at entrance). Book dinner reservations in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning resort wellness day. Begin with a 7:00 AM guided breathwork and meditation session. Then indulge in the resort spa's signature 'Royal Bali Ritual' – a 3-hour immersive treatment including a full-body scrub with Balinese spices, a floral milk bath, and a traditional four-hand massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a peaceful afternoon at the resort's private beach. Take a stand-up paddleboard lesson or simply lounge in a private cabana with a good book. Arrange a personalized afternoon tea service on your villa terrace with the resort's pastry chef's creations.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-villa dining experience – the resort chef comes to your suite to prepare and serve a bespoke Balinese feast in the privacy of your beachfront villa, complete with traditional decorations and a curated wine selection.

meals.breakfast: Balinese-inspired breakfast in bed – nasi goreng, fresh tropical fruits, jamu shots, and Balinese kopi
meals.lunch: Afternoon tea service on villa terrace – finger sandwiches, premium pastries, scones with clotted cream, and fine teas
meals.dinner: Private in-villa chef's dinner – bespoke 6-course Balinese tasting menu with wine pairing, served in your suite

day_by_day.notes: This is a dedicated rest and wellness day. Pre-book the 3-hour spa ritual at least 2 days ahead. In-villa dining must be arranged with the concierge by noon on the same day.

day_by_day.morning: Private chauffeured day trip to Ubud – Bali's cultural heartland. Begin with a visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary. Then explore the Ubud Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung) and the vibrant Ubud Art Market for premium Balinese handicrafts, silk, and artwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a private guided tour of the stunning Tegallalang Rice Terraces – one of Bali's most photographed landscapes. Afterward, visit a premium Balinese coffee plantation for a guided luwak coffee tasting experience. Stop at a renowned local art gallery in Ubud.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong or Barong dance performance at Ubud Palace. Dine at Locavore – one of Bali's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants, celebrated for its farm-to-table philosophy and innovative Indonesian tasting menus (advance reservation essential).

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before departure – fresh fruits, yogurt, granola, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bridges Bali or Mozaic Restaurant in Ubud – contemporary cuisine in a stunning jungle gorge setting
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Locavore, Ubud – Indonesia's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant, featuring hyper-local, seasonal ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Locavore requires reservations weeks in advance – book immediately. The drive from the resort to Ubud takes approximately 60–90 minutes. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the rice terraces.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga and mindfulness session at 7:00 AM. After breakfast, enjoy a private guided surfing lesson on one of Bali's beginner-friendly waves near the resort – July brings consistent, clean swells to Bali's southwestern coast. Professional instructors and premium equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon. Enjoy a private 'Couples Yoga and Sound Healing' session at the resort's yoga shala – combining restorative yoga poses with Tibetan singing bowls and sound therapy for deep relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local beach town near the resort – browse boutique shops, local galleries, and artisan stores. Enjoy sundowners at a premium nearby beach bar before returning to the resort for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Protein-rich pre-surf breakfast – scrambled eggs, avocado, whole grain toast, fresh juices, and smoothies at the resort
meals.lunch: Post-surf healthy lunch at the resort's pool bar – grilled fish, quinoa salads, coconut water, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant – fresh catch of the day, premium steaks, and a curated wine list under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Surfing lessons are suitable for all levels – inform the instructor of your experience level. Sound healing session requires advance booking through the resort's wellness team.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Nusa Penida – Bali's most spectacular island neighbor. Depart by private speed boat from Sanur Beach. Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach (T-Rex cliff viewpoint), one of the most photographed spots in all of Southeast Asia. Hike to the viewpoint for breathtaking panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nusa Penida – visit the stunning Angel's Billabong natural infinity pool and Broken Beach (Pasih Uug), a natural archway carved by the ocean into dramatic limestone cliffs. Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and coral.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private speedboat to the mainland. Enjoy a relaxing resort dinner and an evening wind-down with a private 60-minute foot and leg reflexology massage at the spa.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure – full buffet spread with Balinese specialties, eggs, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium local warung or beach restaurant on Nusa Penida – fresh grilled fish, lobster, and tropical drinks
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at the resort's restaurant – lighter fare such as fresh sashimi, grilled vegetables, and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Nusa Penida day trip is full and active – wear comfortable shoes with grip for cliff paths. Book the private speedboat in advance. Bring motion sickness medication if needed – the crossing can be choppy. SPF 50+ essential.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle morning restorative yoga and pranayama session at 7:30 AM – a recovery practice after the active Nusa Penida day. After breakfast, enjoy a private cooking class at the resort or at a nearby premium culinary studio – learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes including satay lilit, black rice pudding, and lawar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby premium beach club for a luxurious afternoon – reserve a private daybed or cabana, swim in the pool, and enjoy premium cocktails and light bites. Alternatively, return to the resort for a relaxing spa afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional Balinese blessing ceremony arranged by the resort – a deeply spiritual and culturally immersive experience led by a local Balinese priest at a nearby temple. Return for a fine-dining dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast – smoothie bowls, overnight oats, fresh fruits, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes you prepared during the cooking class as part of the culinary experience
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort – chef's special menu featuring seasonal Balinese ingredients with a premium cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Balinese blessing ceremony is a respectful, authentic cultural experience – dress modestly and follow the priest's guidance. The cooking class is typically 3–4 hours including eating the prepared meal.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga at 6:30 AM – a dynamic vinyasa flow to energize the day. After breakfast, embark on a private guided cycling tour through the scenic countryside near the resort – ride through local villages, rice paddies, and coconut groves with a knowledgeable guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Balinese healer (Balian) for a unique wellness consultation – an authentic cultural experience that has been part of Balinese life for centuries (as made famous by 'Eat Pray Love'). Arrange through the concierge for a vetted, respectful experience. Return to the resort for a relaxing swim.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury sunset sailing cruise on a private catamaran – sail along Bali's coastline as the sun dips below the horizon, with champagne, canapés, and a private crew. Return to shore for a late dinner at a premium nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pre-cycling energizing breakfast – banana pancakes, protein smoothies, boiled eggs, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local warung during the cycling tour – authentic Balinese nasi campur in a traditional village setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuca Restaurant (Jimbaran) or equivalent – innovative tapas-style cuisine using local Balinese ingredients in a chic, contemporary setting

day_by_day.notes: The cycling tour is moderately active – inform the guide of your fitness level. The Balian healer visit is optional and deeply personal – the concierge can recommend a highly regarded and authentic practitioner. Book the catamaran sunset cruise 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning yoga immersion – a 90-minute special yoga and meditation workshop with the resort's senior instructor, focusing on integration and mindfulness. After yoga, enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast on your villa terrace overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on the resort's private beach – swim, snorkel, or simply relax in a luxury cabana with a cocktail and a book. Arrange a final luxury 90-minute 'Farewell Bali' spa treatment – a deeply relaxing combination of traditional Balinese massage and aromatherapy.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – request a special table on the beach or at the best table in the house. Celebrate the journey with a premium degustation menu and a bottle of champagne. After dinner, enjoy a stargazing session on the private beach.

meals.breakfast: Lavish final breakfast on the villa terrace – fresh-baked pastries, smoked salmon, tropical fruits, Balinese coffee, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort cabana bar – fresh ceviche, sashimi, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Premium farewell degustation dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – 7-course tasting menu with champagne and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the farewell dinner table in advance and inform the concierge it is your last evening – the resort may arrange special touches such as floral decorations or a personalized dessert. Pack non-essentials tonight to ease departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the private beach – a quiet, reflective moment to savour the last morning in Bali. Enjoy a final yoga session or a peaceful beach walk. Indulge in a leisurely last breakfast at the resort before checking out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit a nearby luxury boutique or spa for any last-minute shopping or treatments. The resort concierge can arrange a private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport at the appropriate time.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with memories of an extraordinary 13-day luxury journey. The private transfer ensures a seamless, comfortable journey to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final farewell breakfast at the resort – a full spread of your favourite dishes from the trip, enjoyed slowly before check-out
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a nearby café before departure
meals.dinner: Inflight dining or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 noon – request a late check-out if your flight allows. The resort's concierge team will assist with luggage storage if needed between check-out and your transfer. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures.

query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA
